To determine which phase is responsible for each ordering, we prepared as-cast Fe 27 Co 27 Ni 17 Ti 29 , corresponding to Fe 27.3 Co 26.6 Ni 17.4 Ti 28.7 of the C14 phase in FeCoNiTi, using an analogous procedure.
As anticipated, Fe 27 Co 27 Ni 17 Ti 29 is predominantly composed of the C14 phase.
Comparing the magnetic properties of FeCoNiTi and Fe 27 Co 27 Ni 17 Ti 29 elucidates which phase is responsible for the respective ordering temperatures.

The comparison of χ dc ( T ) between FeCoNiTi and C14 phase dominant Fe 27 Co 27 Ni 17 Ti 29 suggests that the FM orderings at T c = 1084 and 168 K occur in the fcc phase and that at T c = 214 K is induced by the C14 phase
Subsequently, assuming that the H dependence of M ( M ( H )) of the C14 phase mirrors that of Fe 27 Co 27 Ni 17 Ti 29 , M ( H ) of the fcc phase at a fixed temperature can be computed
Figure 3 a shows the χ dc ( T ) of Fe 27 Co 27 Ni 17 Ti 29 , dominated by the C14 phase, measured under H of 100 Oe.

research_thread.scientific_problem: Deconvoluting the magnetic origins of multiple ferromagnetic transitions in the dual-phase FeCoNiTi high-entropy alloy to identify the specific phase responsible for the low-temperature 58 K anomaly.
research_thread.material_system: FeCoNiTi High-Entropy Alloy (HEA) with fcc and C14 Laves phases.
research_thread.sample_lineage: Original dual-phase as-cast FeCoNiTi (Vfcc:Vc14 = 57:43) and synthesized Fe 27 Co 27 Ni 17 Ti 29 (C14-dominant).
research_thread.intervention: Synthesis of an alloy composition matching the C14 phase to isolate its magnetic properties from the fcc phase.
research_thread.baseline: Dual-phase FeCoNiTi where transitions at 1084, 214, and 168 K are observed, with attribution to fcc and C14 phases.
research_thread.conditions: Temperature range 50 K to 400 K; Magnetic field 100 Oe.
research_thread.structure: Hexagonal C14 (dominant) and Face-Centered Cubic (minor) phases in the synthesized sample.
research_thread.outcome: Three magnetic anomalies observed at 246, 183, and 58 K. The 58 K anomaly is hypothesized to be from the parasitic fcc phase.
research_thread.mechanism: The C14 phase governs higher temperature ordering (attributed to 214 K in baseline, 246/183 K in dominant sample), while the fcc phase is responsible for lower temperature transitions (168 K in baseline, 58 K in dominant sample).
research_thread.hypothesis_value: Confirms that phase separation and composition control are critical for understanding magnetic properties in multi-phase HEAs; identifies the parasitic fcc phase as the source of low-T magnetism.
alternative_explanations: The 58 K transition could be an intrinsic property of the C14 phase if the composition is slightly off or defects are present.
The fcc phase might undergo a different type of magnetic ordering than ferromagnetism.
null_or_negative_results: The 58 K anomaly persists even in the C14-dominant sample, contradicting a pure C14 model.
missing_information: Exact volume fraction of the parasitic fcc phase in the synthesized sample.
Composition of the parasitic fcc phase in the synthesized sample.
Quantitative magnetization data to compare experimental vs. theoretical C14 values.
